# Methodology

**Current experiment:** a user-authorized synthetic demonstration generated by `src.generate_synthetic`. Labels follow the documented recipe, not independent annotations; all metrics refer to that generator. See `docs/synthetic_dataset.md`.

SpendSense Campus addresses two distinct problems: supervised classification of short expense descriptions and transparent arithmetic for a student's recorded budget. Only the former uses machine learning. Amount, date, saved category corrections and spending history never become classification inputs automatically.

## Reproducible experiment

1. Verify a labelled source and manifest. Inspect exact filenames, headers, class counts, missing values and provenance. Hash the original CSV.
2. Normalize Unicode (NFKC) and whitespace while preserving merchant punctuation, digits, accents and case. Detect duplicates using a casefolded key. Remove invalid text/labels, all conflicting exact-description groups, and same-label repeated descriptions. Record every excluded source row and reason. No stemming or stop-word removal.
3. Split the resulting unique descriptions once, stratified, approximately 80/20, seed 42. At least two classes and five unique descriptions per class are required. Save source row IDs and the holdout checksum. Exact normalized descriptions never overlap.
4. Fit a separate scikit-learn Pipeline per classifier. TF-IDF uses word unigrams/bigrams, sublinear term frequency, L2 normalization, up to 20,000 training-fitted features, and one-character-or-longer tokens. Vocabulary and IDF are learned inside each training CV fold. Test words never alter these choices.
5. Use 2–5 stratified training-only CV folds, bounded by the smallest class. Tune Logistic Regression C ∈ {0.5, 2}, Multinomial NB alpha ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1}, Linear SVM C ∈ {0.5, 2}, and Tree depth ∈ {12, 30}, minimum leaf size ∈ {2, 5}, pruning alpha ∈ {0, 0.001}. Grids and feature policy are fixed in code, not adapted to test scores. Linear optimizers have explicit iteration limits; convergence warnings trigger one higher-limit retry, then a clear failure.
6. Select the model with the highest mean **training CV macro-F1**, then refit on the primary training partition. Ties follow declared model order. Save all four fitted pipelines. Do not select the apparent highest test scorer. Do not refit on test records.
7. Evaluate all four models on the exact same holdout records, report accuracy, macro/weighted precision, recall and F1, per-class scores, confusion matrices, fit/tuning time and batch prediction latency. ROC-AUC is omitted; it is not needed for the required comparison and no calibration experiment is performed.
8. Count overlap of simple template groups (casefolded descriptions with digit runs replaced and punctuation collapsed). Where repeated groups and class support permit, run a separate five-fold-derived grouped holdout and independently grouped CV-tune all four models on its training groups. This sensitivity evaluation never changes the primary selected model. Save its split and metrics, or an explicit reason why it cannot run. Templates are not merchant identities; semantic near-duplicates can still remain.

## Four classifiers

**Logistic Regression:** L2-regularized linear classifier; multinomial learning is handled by scikit-learn's multiclass solver. Distributed sparse word evidence often suits text. Its probabilities are uncalibrated.

**Multinomial Naive Bayes:** models class-conditional feature counts with additive smoothing; accepts nonnegative TF-IDF as weighted count-like inputs. Fast and simple, but the conditional independence assumption is imperfect and probabilities can be overconfident.

**Linear SVM:** learns separating hyperplanes with regularization. It exposes signed decision scores; these are not probabilities. No second classifier or probability wrapper is introduced.

**Decision Tree:** recursively partitions sparse TF-IDF features. Depth, leaf size and pruning limit complexity. Sparse high-dimensional text offers many possible local splits; a tree may fragment examples and generalize less well than distributed linear evidence. This is a methodological expectation, not an observed result before training. Plots truncate at three levels and rules at five for readability.

## Metrics and uncertainty

Precision measures the correctness of a class's positive predictions; recall measures how many actual examples it retrieves. F1 is their harmonic mean. Macro-F1 averages class F1 equally and is primary because rare expense categories matter. Weighted scores weight by class support and can obscure minority failures; accuracy measures the fraction correct overall. Undefined per-class ratios are set to zero and support counts remain visible.

Review is recommended when maximum probability < 0.60 (LR/NB/Tree), or the SVM margin < 0.50 (top-two score gap for multiclass; absolute boundary distance for binary). These fixed heuristics are not validated error guarantees and are not tuned on the test set. An all-zero TF-IDF input always requires review. Tree leaf estimates can be particularly poorly calibrated. Confidence values across models are not interchangeable. Displayed recognized terms indicate feature coverage, not causal explanations.

## Budget calculations

Let S be recorded month-to-date spending, B the budget and D remaining calendar days including today. Remaining = max(0, B − S), overspend = max(0, S − B), and daily allowance = remaining / D when D > 0. Month-end pace estimate = S / elapsed calendar days × month length. Today counts in both elapsed and remaining periods. Drift = S − B × elapsed days / month length.

For a past month, daily allowance is unavailable and projection equals actual recorded total. Before a future month begins, allowance divides the full budget by month length and projection is unavailable. Zero budgets are valid; missing budgets are explicitly unset. Amounts persist as integer cents/paise using decimal half-up rounding. The app supports one currency, INR; it performs no currency conversion. Irregular payments and unrecorded expenses can distort all estimates.

## Privacy and boundaries

Records stay in local SQLite. Parameterized SQL, batch validation, spreadsheet-safe exports and Git exclusions protect common workflows. Model files, derived text and tree vocabulary remain local and ignored. SQLite is not encrypted; the application has no multi-user authentication and binds to localhost. Load only locally generated Joblib files because pickle-based loading can execute code. Do not enter banking credentials or personal identifiers. Corrections remain bookkeeping data; no automatic retraining or cloud services are used.
